records.name: Buenos Aires
records.summary:
Buenos Aires Province carries the strongest sub-national negative signal in the country: the provincial human-rights ombudsman's 2016 submission to the UN Human Rights Committee documents acts of violence, persecution and harassment by provincial police — or by third parties under police cover — against trans and travesti people during operations in three cities (La Plata, Mar del Plata and Esteban Echeverría), under 'preventive policing' frameworks. Academic legal analysis confirms that after the 2012 Gender Identity Law formally decriminalised trans presence, security forces increased use of drug-law prosecution — devolved to provincial justice in 2005 — and street-offence law as the operative instrument of indirect criminalisation of travesti/trans identity: a patterned, state-implicated escalation.

sources.summary: Buenos Aires provincial ombudsman's Gender Violence Office (created by Resolución Nº 100/10) submission to the UN Human Rights Committee (June-July 2016 review): documents violence, persecution and harassment by provincial police — or third parties under police cover — against trans and travesti people in Buenos Aires province, in a dedicated section on violence by judicial, state and police agents. This is the record's core 2016 UN-submission claim. Note: 2016-17 UN-review PDFs no longer describe current law — the 2012 federal Gender Identity Law remains in force, but a Dec-2024 national DNU added consent/medical-judicial requirements for minors' gender-affirming care (under litigation).

UNLP thesis documenting the criminalisation of trans and travesti women in Buenos Aires province through drug-offence prosecutions under microtrafficking enforcement, focused on La Plata's Zona Roja — showing that after the 2012 Gender Identity Law formally decriminalised trans presence, security-led street-offence policing became the operative indirect-criminalisation instrument in the province. Regional academic evidence for the record's escalation claim.

Pensamiento Penal legal analysis: rising criminalisation of trans/travesti women in Buenos Aires province, particularly La Plata's Zona Roja, and it records that in 2005 Buenos Aires province assumed jurisdiction over drug-sale and possession offences — the devolution that enabled provincial street-offence and drug-law prosecution as the indirect-criminalisation instrument. Supplies the dated 2005 mechanism behind the record's escalation claim.

Provincial Ombudsman's September 2024 guide to gender-marker rectification for people born in Buenos Aires province: registry rectification steps, including provisions for people born in the province now living elsewhere. Dated local procedure evidence — provincial implementation of the 2012 federal Gender Identity Law's recognition regime.

records.name: Subcarpathian Voivodeship
records.summary:
For a trans traveler the exposure here is social rather than statutory: the local anti-LGBT declarations were never criminal statutes, and every such document in the country had been repealed or invalidated by 24 April 2025, when the county charter that was the country's final surviving holdout was repealed at an extraordinary session; this state/province's own resolution had been repealed on 20 September 2021.

Practical safety is the operative concern: the repeal was forced from outside (the European Commission threatened to withhold regional development funds) rather than produced by a change in local attitudes, so the de facto social climate that generated the resolutions is assessed to persist. Being visibly trans at a public event in an eastern town whose local authority resisted all external pressure until 2025 carries harassment exposure, and the record shows executive intent to exclude a visible LGBTQ public presence - the capital's mayor banned the 2019 equality march on security grounds, the district court overturned the ban, and the march proceeded.

sources.summary: Notes from Poland (27 Apr 2025): the county of Łańcut in southeast Poland (Podkarpackie) — the last local authority in the country with an anti-LGBT resolution — repealed the measure at an extraordinary councillors' session, closing the resolution era; at the wave's peak about one third of Poland's territory was covered by such documents (per the Atlas of Hate mapping project). Dated end-point for the record's 'last holdout' claim.

The Them (23 Sep 2021, updated 29 Sep): Podkarpackie's voivodeship council repealed its 'LGBT-free' resolution on Monday 20 September 2021, alongside Małopolska and Lubelskie — after the European Commission threatened to withhold regional development funds; Podkarpackie replaced its ordinance with a generic anti-discrimination statement. Confirms the record's 2021 voivodeship repeal under EU funding pressure.
